text:
The Blue Jackets have been slumping, and Adam Fantilli has taken some of the heat. Yahoo Sports argued that treating him as a scapegoat is the wrong thing to do, and after the loss to the Islanders, The Hockey Writers wrote about Columbus limiting him; he played 13 minutes that night.

Our numbers side with the defense. He plays 20:21 a night and has 65 shots and 7.95 expected goals (the quality of his chances) in 21 games. Seven goals is a little light for those looks, and his 10.8% shooting sits below his likely range near 12%. Then he answered: two points against Chicago, with 1.62 expected goals that night alone, and two more with eight shots in the comeback win in Toronto.

The real concern is the other end. With him on the ice Columbus gets 46.7% of the five-on-five expected goals, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him out there last season (bottom 6% of forwards). The upside is just as clear in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: 93rd percentile for chances from in front of the net, and he carries the puck in on 58% of his entries.
headline: Adam Fantilli is getting the chances, and the blame
